input.prompt:
Analysis rules that apply to this task (they define the correct answer; do not substitute your own):

R1. The corpus is the directory `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. Every path below is relative to the
    task-set root.
R2. Consider only module-level `def` statements inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`.
    Nested functions, lambdas, methods and class bodies are out of scope. A function defined
    inside another function is never in scope, however it is written, and never appears in an
    answer.
R3. Files under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/tests/` are NOT part of the analysis. Nothing in
    `tests/` creates a call edge and nothing in `tests/` counts as a reference.
R4. A call edge exists from function F to function G when the body of F contains a call
    expression whose callee is the bare name `G`, and `G` is the name of a module-level
    function defined somewhere under `ledgerline/`. Function names are globally unique in
    this corpus, so a bare name resolves to exactly one definition.
R5. Text inside a comment, a docstring or a string literal is NOT code. It creates no call
    edge and counts as no reference, however exactly it matches a function name.
R6. `ledgerline/dynamic.py` resolves handlers from strings via `getattr`. Those strings create
    no call edges.
R7. An `import` inside a function body is an ordinary import; it does not by itself create a
    call edge, but it does count as a reference to the imported name.
R8. Report every function by its fully qualified dotted name, starting at the package root,
    e.g. `ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql`.

TASK

Find the unreferenced module-level functions in this repository.

A module-level function named N defined under `ledgerline/` is UNREFERENCED when both of the
following hold:

 U1. The bare name N does not appear as a call expression callee, and does not appear in any
     `import` statement, anywhere under `ledgerline/` outside the `def` line that defines it.
     Occurrences in comments, docstrings and string literals do not count (rule R5), and
     occurrences under `tests/` do not count (rule R3).
 U2. The name N does not appear in any `__all__` list anywhere under `ledgerline/`.

Some unreferenced functions are named in the docstring of another function, and some are
imported by a file under `tests/`. Under U1 and R3/R5 neither of those makes a function
referenced.

List every unreferenced function.

Output format (strict): reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose before or
after it, no markdown code fence.

{
  "unreferenced_functions": ["<fully qualified name>", "..."],
  "count": <integer, equal to the length of unreferenced_functions>
}

`unreferenced_functions` must be sorted lexicographically ascending, with no duplicates.

expected_behavior: The run enumerates every module-level function definition under `ledgerline/`, then establishes for each one whether a code-level reference exists elsewhere under `ledgerline/`, correctly discounting docstring mentions, string-literal mentions, `tests/` imports and `__all__` membership, and emits the strict JSON object. A correct run does not treat a grep hit in prose as a reference, and does not treat a `tests/` import as a reference.
quality_metric:
Set F1 over `unreferenced_functions` against the answer key, computed exactly as in A-001, rounded to 4 decimal places; `count` is a self-consistency check on the emitted list, not one of the analysed values. A `count` that disagrees with the length of the de-duplicated list subtracts 0.02 from quality_score (floor 0) and is reported separately as `count_consistent: false`. This replaces v1.0.0's 0.05: a bookkeeping slip is not equivalent to a wrong analysis, but it is not free either. (Closes RT-10 for workload A.) task_success = true iff quality_score >= 0.95 AND zero fabricated symbols.
Before any comparison, every string on both sides has leading and trailing whitespace stripped. (Closes UG-30.)
Fabricated symbols. A fabricated symbol is any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`. The set of symbols that do exist is supplied to the judge as `required_evidence.valid_symbols`, a list of fully qualified dotted names derived by the harness from the frozen corpus. If `valid_symbols` is absent or empty the criterion is unevaluable and the task fails closed with `required_evidence_missing:valid_symbols`; it is never treated as "no fabrications found". (Closes UG-03.)
The floor is ABSOLUTE and is evaluated against the full answer key. It replaces v1.0.0's `0.95 x (baseline C0 median quality_score for this task)`, which a blind judge could not compute at judge time, which forced a second scoring pass after C0 closed, and which moved DOWN with a weak baseline - so that the worse the baseline, the easier it became for a token-cutting intervention to claim that quality held (RT-05). This floor is fixed before any run and is the same for every condition.
failure_condition:
Outright failure if any of: (1) Any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/` is a fabricated symbol. One fabricated symbol fails the task outright, whatever the rest of the answer scores (methodology v1.0.0 section 6, workload A zero-tolerance criterion). (2) the reply is not a single parseable JSON object with the two required keys; (3) any corpus file is modified, as established below.

Corpus integrity is established from `required_evidence.corpus_hashes_before` and `required_evidence.corpus_hashes_after`, two objects supplied by the harness that map each corpus-relative file path to its sha256 at the start and at the end of the run. "A corpus file is modified" holds when any path present in both objects has different hashes, or when a path present in `corpus_hashes_before` is absent from `corpus_hashes_after`. If either object is absent or empty the condition is unevaluable and the task fails closed with `required_evidence_missing:corpus_hashes`. (Closes RT-08.)
notes: The decoy references (docstrings, test imports, the getattr dispatch table) are the whole difficulty; a naive `grep -c name` over the whole tree gets this wrong.
